bus_p3_r3: A new roommate doesn't win you over with a speech on move-in day. The rent just has to keep showing up. Your Protector, the grown-up you, earns that protective part's trust about the same way, mostly out in ordinary life. The things you do can be small, like keeping a promise to yourself nobody else knew about. Or saying no to someone, and not texting an hour later to take it back. That second one can be really hard.
bus_p4_r3: You could tell that part, "You can stay right there and watch, and I'll stop if it gets to be too much." Most protective parts can live with a deal like that, and it keeps you to one small step at a time. And if it says no? Then it's no. When it does let you go on, follow whatever changes. A critic that kept saying "This is stupid" might soften into "I'm scared to get my hopes up." That one's easier to be kind to.
bus_p5_r3a: So talk to whatever's showing up. If the critic turned into somebody scared, that's who you're talking to now, no need to go back to square one and look for your little one. Maybe a vague hurt turns out to be about wanting someone on your side for once. Oof. If it does, try being that someone. You could even say it out loud: "I'm on your side." It may feel silly to say out loud. Notice how it lands anyway. You don't need to know how old you were, or what happened, to do that. A small shift counts, and more intensity isn't the only way forward. Sometimes all that happens is your shoulders come down a little.
